scope: v5 two-model formal score root, formal result report, Section 21 contract appendix, run audit provenance, and both detailed failure-analysis JSON sidecars
method_note: Windows long-path-aware System.IO access (\\?\ prefix) was used for score-root sidecars. Legacy path APIs falsely reported the long paths as absent; this is not a data-artifact failure.

findings.finding: detailed_failure_analysis_gpt41_v1.json and detailed_failure_analysis_gpt54_v1.json both exist, are readable, and parse as JSON when accessed with the Windows long-path prefix.

checks.name: Required JSON validity
checks.result: All eight artifacts parse as JSON; the two detailed-analysis JSON sidecars required long-path-aware access.

checks.name: Overall score recomputation from the 48 adopted records
checks.result: Matches the aggregate, metric artifact, result JSON, and published report values.

checks.name: All reported metric partitions
checks.result: Independent recomputation matched every model, stage, use-case, model-stage, and model-use-case cell in metrics_by_model_stage_case_v5.json and every model/stage/model-stage cell in formal_aggregate_v5.json, including hits, denominators, false-positive types, and rates.

checks.name: Atomic alignment negatives
checks.result: Every Gold subject/operation/object score was checked against included adopted TP matched_gold_item_id coverage.

checks.name: Targeted third-review and adjudication reconciliation
checks.result: All 47 adjudication-manifest targets exist in the adopted ledger and each adopted decision/score matches. review3 count and run/gold-hash validations are PASS.

checks.name: Detailed failure-analysis sidecar consistency
checks.result: Both JSON sidecars agree with the adopted ledger, metric artifacts, formal result report, and their readable Markdown counterparts.

checks.name: Provenance hashes
checks.result: Matches merge_validation_v5.json, adjudication_manifest_v5.json, and the source-binding manifest where applicable.

checks.name: Report claim scope
checks.result: Gold statements are bounded to traceability and absence of a clear defect explaining the observed misses; they do not claim universal Gold truth. Normal-versus-attack discussion explicitly says case count, chain length, model, and repetitions differ, and prohibits treating numerical differences as an attack-only causal effect.

conclusion: PASS. No numerical, denominator, rate, adjudication, atomic-consistency, failure-count, resource, provenance, JSON-validity, or claim-scope mismatch was found.
